subject: general
question: If a train travelling at a speed of 90 km/h crosses a pole in 5 sec, then the length of train is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Speed** in m/s = 90 × (5/18) = 25 m/s.

**Length of train** = **Speed** × **Time**.

**Length** = 25 × 5 = 125 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 125 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed** of train = 90 km/h

**Time** taken to cross the **pole** = 5 sec

**Formula Used:**

**Distance** = **Speed** × **Time**

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5ca6dfb130e55b5bfa761db23c589641474cd3ee00ce707df9d435ee2398ce70.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Speed** in m/s = 90 × (5/18) m/s

⇒ **Speed** = 5 × 5 = 25 m/s

⇒ **Length of train** (Distance) = 25 m/s × 5 sec

⇒ **Length** = 125 m

**∴ The correct answer is 125 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing a Stationary Object

When a train crosses a **pole** or a **standing man**, the distance covered is equal to the **length of the train**.

Crossing a Platform

When a train crosses a **platform** or **bridge** of length P, total distance = **Length of train** + **P**.</p
